TI Cardioprotective Effect of Apigenin-Hydroxyapatite Nanocomposite against
   H2O2-Induced Injury in Cardiomyoblast Cells
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Apigenin; Cardiovascular Disease; Hydroxyapatite; Myocardial Injury;
   Cardiomyoblast
ID INSIGHTS
AB Background: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide, largely driven by oxidative stress and inflammation during myocardial ischemia and reperfusion injury. Apigenin, a natural flavonoid, exhibits potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties but suffers from poor solubility and bioavailability. To overcome these limitations, a novel Apigenin-Hydroxyapatite Nanocomposite (Api-HANPs) was developed to enhance its therapeutic efficacy against oxidative cardiac injury. Materials and Methods: Api-HANPs were synthesized via a green mechanochemical approach and characterized using FTIR, XRD, and FESEM analyses to confirm composite formation and structural morphology. The cardioprotective potential of Api-HANPs was evaluated in H9c2 cardiomyoblast cells exposed to Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)-induced oxidative stress. Cytotoxicity, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT), lipid peroxidation (MDA), intracellular Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) levels, apoptosis (AO/EB, DAPI), and mitochondrial membrane potential (Rh-123) were assessed. Molecular docking was performed to explore apigenin's binding affinity with the NF-kappa B protein, and immunofluorescence staining was used to evaluate NF-kappa B and Nrf2 nuclear translocation. Results: FTIR and XRD confirmed successful integration of apigenin into the hydroxyapatite matrix with altered crystallinity and improved surface morphology. Api-HANPs markedly improved cell viability in a dose-dependent manner, with maximal protection at 50 & micro;M. Pretreatment with Api-HANPs significantly reduced H2O2-induced apoptosis, ROS production, and MDA levels while restoring antioxidant enzyme activity and mitochondrial membrane potential (p < 0.0001). Molecular docking revealed a strong binding affinity between apigenin and NF-kappa B (-7.7 kcal/mol), and immunostaining showed that Api-HANPs suppressed NF-kappa B nuclear translocation while promoting Nrf2 activation, indicating simultaneous anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions. Conclusion: The Api-HANPs nanocomposite effectively mitigates oxidative stress-induced cardiomyoblast injury by restoring redox balance, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and modulating NF-kappa B/Nrf2 signaling pathways. These findings suggest Api-HANPs as a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for preventing oxidative cardiac damage and managing cardiovascular disorders.

TI Development and Optimization of a Super Saturable Self-Nanoemulsifying
   Drug Delivery System for Ibrutinib: Enhancing Solubility and Anticancer
   Potential
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Super saturable SNEDDS; Ibrutinib; Box-Behnken design; Nanocarriers;
   Drug solubility; Cytotoxicity; Cell lines
ID IN-VITRO; DESIGN; SNEDDS; FORMULATION; INHIBITOR; MIXTURES
AB Aim: This study explores the development and optimization of a Super saturable Self-Nanoemulsifying Drug Delivery System to enhance the solubility, bioavailability, and anticancer efficacy of ibrutinib. Materials and Methods: Saturation solubility studies identified Kolliphor (R) RH 40, castor oil, and PEG-600 as the optimal surfactant, oil, and co-surfactant, respectively. Formulation optimization was performed using a Box-Behnken design, with droplet size and encapsulation efficiency as key response variables. Characterization included particle size analysis, zeta potential, FTIR, DSC, and XRPD studies, while in vitro drug release was assessed through diffusion studies. The MTT assay on MCF-7 and PANC-1 cell lines evaluated the cytotoxicity and therapeutic potential of the formulation. Results: The optimized S-SNEDDS for Ibrutinib demonstrated favorable characteristics, including a small droplet size (71.12-76.38 nm), high encapsulation efficiency (61.56-87.22%), and stability under stress conditions. The formulation exhibited rapid drug release, with over 50% of Ibrutinib released within 240 min. Characterization studies, including FTIR and DSC, confirmed the amorphous nature of the encapsulated drug. Kinetic studies suggested a zero-order drug release mechanism. Cytotoxicity evaluation via MTT assay indicated that the nanoformulation had lower cytotoxicity on MCF-7 and PANC-1 cells compared to pure Ibrutinib . Conclusion: These findings underscore the potential of S-SNEDDS as a promising approach to enhance the oral bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs like ibrutinib.

TI Novel and Simple LC-MS/MS Technique for the Simultaneous Quantitation of
   Metformin and Remogliflozin in Rat Plasma
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Acetonitrile; LC-MS/MS; ICH; Metformin; Remogliflozin; Simultaneous
   quantitation.
ID TANDEM MASS-SPECTROMETRY; QUANTIFICATION; SITAGLIPTIN; VALIDATION
AB Background: Metformin and remogliflozin in fixed dose combination prescribe to control blood sugar and avoid long term complication associated with diabetes mellitus. Aim: The aim is to establish a straightforward and sensitive bioanalytical method as well as to validate LC/ MS-MS technique for the concurrent quantitative determination of metformin and remogliflozin in rat plasma. Materials and Methods: The analytical separation of analytes with contrast physicochemical properties was successfully performed with C18 column (BDS Hypersil, 150 x 4.6 phase was composed of 10 mM ammonium acetate dissolved in Milli-Q water (pH 7) (25%) and acetonitrile (75%) (v/v) at 0.7 mL/min flow through isocratic elution. A 10 & micro;L injection volume was utilized in a brief run time of 4 min. Results and Discussion: Developed LC-MS/MS technique has been validated as per ICH guidelines (ICH M10). The validation data showed a precise, accurate, selective method and recovery and stability falling within the acceptable limits. Conclusion: A meticulous, precise, and repeatable LC-MS/MS method employing liquid-liquid extraction has been developed for concurrent quantitation of metformin and remogliflozin in rat plasma. The benefits provided by this method in terms of plasma sample requirement for processing as well as improved both sensitivity and reproducibility. The established method is set to be employed for the simultaneous pharmacokinetic analysis of both analytes within a biological matrix.

TI Lentinula edodes Polysaccharides Inhibit Estrogen Biosynthesis Enzymes
   in Hormone-Dependent Breast Cancer
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Lentinula edodes; Breast Cancer; Natural products; Estrogen biosynthesis
   Enzymes
ID 17-BETA-HYDROXYSTEROID-DEHYDROGENASE IMPAIRS; AROMATASE; ESTRADIOL
AB Background / Objective: Breast cancer, a leading cause of death among women, is closely associated with estrogen metabolism. This study investigated the potential of partially purified polysaccharides from Lentinula edodes (shiitake mushroom) as natural inhibitors of key enzymes involved in estrogen production aromatase, estrone sulfatase, and 17 beta hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase which are vital in the progression of hormone-dependent breast cancer. Materials and Methods: Polysaccharide fractions were purified using ion-exchange and size-exclusion chromatography. Enzyme inhibition was assessed through ELISA and colorimetric assays, which revealed concentration-dependent inhibition, with the highest activity observed at 400 & micro;g/mL: aromatase (87.25%, IC50=181.25 & micro;g/mL), estrone sulfatase (86.62%, IC50=187.5 & micro;g/mL), and 17 beta hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (86.67%, IC50=208.4 & micro;g/mL). GC-MS analysis identified 33 bioactive compounds, of which 14 were evaluated for pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness properties using SwissADME. Results: Molecular docking showed strong binding interactions between selected compounds (D-fructose and diethyl mercaptal pentaacetate) and the target enzymes, supporting their inhibitory potential. In silico toxicity predictions further confirmed favorable safety profiles. Conclusion: Collectively, these findings highlight L. edodes-derived polysaccharides and associated bioactive molecules as promising natural inhibitors of estrogen biosynthesis, offering new perspectives for therapeutic strategies against hormone-dependent breast cancer.

TI Evaluation of Toxicity and Anti-Breast Cancer Potential of Methanolic
   Leaf Extract of Anastatica hierochuntica in DMBA Induced

LA English
DT Article
DE Acute and sub-acute toxicity; DMBA; Anti-breast cancer; Anastatica
   hierochuntica
ID INDUCED MAMMARY-CARCINOMA; L.; ASSAY
AB Background: Anastatica hierochuntica has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its therapeutic effects, but its safety and efficacy have not been comprehensively assessed. This study investigated the Methanolic Leaf (ML) extracts of A. hierochuntica acute and sub-acute toxicity in Sprague-Dawley rats and its anti-breast cancer potential in a 7,12-Dimethylbenz[a]Anthracene (DMBA)-induced rat model. Materials and Methods: Acute and sub-acute oral toxicity studies were conducted following the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) guidelines 423 and 407, respectively. Hematological and biochemical parameters were analyzed in blood and serum respectively. Breast tissues were examined for oxidative stress including Lipid Peroxidation (LPO), Catalase (CAT), and Reduced Glutathione (GSH). Histopathological assessments were performed on liver, kidney, spleen, and mammary tissues. The anti-breast cancer study involved DMBA-induced rats treated with ML (200 and 400 mg/ kg) or tamoxifen. Results: The acute toxicity study indicated no treatment-related mortality or significant physiological changes at doses up to 2000 mg/kg. Sub-acute toxicity assessment revealed no adverse effects up to 1000 mg/kg. suggest that ML extract has a high safety profile, with a No-Observed-Adverse-Effect Level (NOAEL) above 1000 mg/kg. In the DMBA-induced model, ML treatment significantly (p<0.05) reduced tumor incidence and tumor weight, with the 400 mg/kg dose showing the greatest efficacy. ML also improved oxidative stress markers by decreasing LPO levels and increasing CAT and GSH activity. Histopathological analysis revealed a reduced tumour burden and improved mammary architecture in ML-treated groups compared to untreated controls. Conclusion: The ML extract of A. hierochuntica demonstrated significant anti-breast cancer potential in DMBA-induced rats, alongside a favourable toxicity profile warranting further investigation for potential therapeutic applications.

ID O/W EMULSIONS; IN-VITRO; ACID; STABILITY
AB Background: Computer vision syndrome is a eye condition linked to long periods of screen use. Early signs include irritation, redness and dryness. Chronic cases can lead to serious issues like high myopia, vitreous floaters and retinal detachment. The study is aimed to create ophthalmic emulsion based on Triphala Ghrita that has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and tissue healing properties. Materials and Methods: The emulsion was made using Triphala Ghrita (oil phase), 0.1% sodium hyaluronate (aqueous phase), Tweens and spans (surfactant) and ethanol (co-surfactant). Permeation studies showed oil phase did not permeate eggshell membrane but using goat corneas the aqueous phase showed a CDR of 9.7% at 30 min and also the oil phase did permeate. Histological analysis confirmed rejuvenation of corneal tissue after treatment with emulsion. Conclusion: The optimized ophthalmic emulsion (E3) showed strong anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory effects, effective corneal penetration and rejuvenation of corneal tissue which highlights its potentials as a treatment for ocular damage due to CVS

TI Development and evaluation of Dry Powder Inhalation Formulation of
   Remdesivir Nanosuspension by Spray Drying Technique
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Remdesivir; Dry Powder Inhalation; Pulmonary Delivery; Spray Drying;
   Solubility Enhancement
AB Introduction: Significant global health issues are caused by respiratory viral infections, such as COVID-19, which call for effective and focused drug delivery methods to improve treatment effectiveness and lessen systemic side effects. The broad-spectrum antiviral Remdesivir has demonstrated potential in treating these infections; however, it has low pulmonary access and poor aqueous solubility when administered by traditional methods. Antivirals can be directly and non-invasively delivered to the lungs, the main site of infection, using Dry Powder Inhaler Pulmonary Drug Delivery System. In order to optimise therapeutic advantages, reduce side effects, and increase local drug concentration, this study attempts to create a DPI formulation of Remdesivir. Objectives:The aim is to formulate and assess a spray-dried Remdesivir DPI for better bioavailability and pulmonary delivery. Materials and Methods: Remdesivir was formulated as a nanosuspension and then spray-dried into particles that could be inhaled in. The powder was comprehensively characterized using Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy, X-ray Powder Diffraction, and Differential Scanning Calorimetry. Solubility enhancement, aerosolisation, and in vitro drug release were evaluated. Results: The particles had a fine particle percentage of 68.84 +/- 4% and a respirable size of 1-5 mu m. Aerosolisation was enhanced by the rough, corrugated surfaces that were visible through SEM. Amorphous conversion was verified by DSC and XRPD, increasing solubility by 17-18 times. Within 150 min, more compared to 70% of the drug was released, and cascade impaction confirmed deep lung deposits. Conclusion: Remdesivir's modified DPI formulation showed improved solubility, effective lung targeting, and prolonged drug release, indicating a high potential for treating viral respiratory infections.

TI Development of Novel RP-HPLC and Chromogenic UV-Visible Methods for the
   Estimation of Sitagliptin Using NQS in Bulk and Biological Samples in
   Compliance with ICH M10 and Q2(R2) Guidelines
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE ICH M10 Guideline; NQS Reagent; RP-HPLC; Sitagliptin; Spectrophotometric
   Method
ID INHIBITOR SITAGLIPTIN; DPP-4 INHIBITOR; PHARMACOKINETICS; VALIDATION;
   STRESS
AB Aim: This study develops and validates two analytical methods: An innovative UV-visible chromogenic spectrophotometric method applied to bio-samples and a (RP-HPLC) High-performance liquid chromatography method in reversed phase to measure sitagliptin in pure and pharmaceutical formulations in compliance with M10 and ICH Q2(R2) criteria. Materials and Methods: Method utilizes a chromogenic reaction, where 1,2-naphthoquinone-4-sulfonate was prepared and optimized as the chromogenic reagent. This reagent reacted with sitagliptin under controlled pH and temperature to produce a coloured product. The resultant chromogen's absorbance was measured spectrophotometrically at its maximum absorption wavelength. Concentration ranges for RP-HPLC were 25-150 & micro;g/mL. Results: Mobile phase for RP-HPLC was made by combining methanol of HPLC grade with potassium dihydrogen phosphate pH 4.3 in 70:30 ratio, 10 min of run time at a flow rate of 1.2 mL/min. Retention time was recorded at 3.41min. Chromogenic method demonstrated a linear response throughout a specific concentration range. calibration curve equation for chromogenic bioanalytical method at 454nm and y=0.0187x+0.0264, R2=0.9998. 5 & micro;g/mL and 100 & micro;g/mL were found to be the Lower Limit of Quantification (LLOQ) followed by Upper Limit of Quantification (ULOQ), respectively for chromogenic method. Conclusion: Both RP-HPLC and chromogenic UV spectrophotometric methods provide rapid as well accurate quantification of sitagliptin in formulations and bulk drug samples. Protein precipitation extraction method was used to design, validate, and expand improved procedure to biological samples. Validation results support their suitability for routine quality control analysis, offering reliable and efficient tools for sitagliptin quantification.

TI Design of Experiments (DoE)-Based Optimization of Pomalidomide
   Nanosuspension for Improved Oral Absorption and Pharmacokinetics
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Pomalidomide; Nanosuspension; Box-Behnken Design; Drug Release;
   Pharmacokinetics
ID THALIDOMIDE
AB Aim: The study aims to enhance the oral bioavailability and solubility of Pomalidomide (POM), which is classified as a class IV medication based on the Biopharmaceutical Classification System (BCS). Materials and Methods: A POM Nanosuspension (NS) was developed using a high-pressure homogenizer. The selection of stabilizers was initially done using a One-Factor-at-A-Time (OFAT) method, considering both PdI and Particle Size (PS). A Box-Behnken Design (BBD) with 3 factors and 3 levels was employed in 17 experimental trials to study how stabilizer concentration, cycle count, and pressure impact Zeta Potential (ZP) and PS. The combination of Soluplus (R) and Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC) was identified as the optimal stabilizer mix. Results: The resulting NS displayed a reduced PS of 132.9 nm and a ZP of -22.9 mV. SEM images showed that the particles were spherical. Further investigation with FT-IR, DSC, and X-ray Diffraction (XRD) studies substantiated the compatibility and alteration of POM into an amorphous state. The optimized POM-NS demonstrated a 21.56-fold increase in solubility, with more than 97% drug release within the first hour. The formulation also showed a 2.14-fold increase in Cmax and a 1.56-fold increase in AUC0-t. Conclusion: The modified POM NS markedly improved solubility, oral absorption, and bioavailability, indicating its potential for higher therapeutic efficacy.

TI Fabrication of a Cost-Effective in-House Electrode Assembly for
   Recording EEG and Behavioral Seizures in Unrestrained Rats

LA English
DT Article

   EEG; Low-Cost Electrode
ID MANAGEMENT
AB Background: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a valuable tool in neuroscience research for analyzing epileptic seizures in animal models. However, the cost that comes with commercial electrode assemblies is a critical challenge, particularly in low- and limited-resource settings. Thus, developing an inexpensive but dependable substitute is critical for improving access to epilepsy pre-clinical research. Materials and Methods: The research article here discusses a systematic methodology for designing and developing a low-cost electrode system for EEG recording and behavioral seizure monitoring in freely moving rats. Results: The stability and performance of internally assembled electrode setup was evaluated during spontaneous and induced seizures in rat models of epilepsy. Our research findings demonstrate that these electrodes were reliable for repeatedly detecting the epileptiform activity, in regards to signal quality and seizure evaluation accuracy. Conclusion: The proposed low-cost electrode structure offers a viable alternative to costly commercial arrangements, making EEG-based seizure analysis more accessible to researchers working within budget restrictions or in limited resource facilities. By providing high-quality EEG recordings and behavioural tests, this method contributes to a better understanding of seizure pathophysiology and supports preclinical research on epilepsy employing animal models.

TI Nanostructured Lipid Carrier-Based Hydrogel of Fenoprofen Calcium for
   Sustained Release: Optimization, Characterisation, and in
   vitro Evaluation
SO INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Fenoprofen Calcium; Box-Behnken design; Nanostructured lipid carriers;
   Sustained drug release
ID BOX-BEHNKEN DESIGN; TOPICAL DELIVERY; EX-VIVO; 888 ATO; GEL;
   NANOPARTICLES; HYDROCHLORIDE; FORMULATION; LIPOSOME
AB Objectives: Fenoprofen Calcium (FEN) has short elimination half-life, frequent dosage administration and numerous gastrointestinal side effects on oral administration. The primary objective of this research was to synthesize optimized FEN-loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carriers (FEN-NLCs) using Box-Behnken design and develop its hydrogel with enhanced dissolution in conjunction with sustained drug release. Materials and Methods: FEN-NLCs were synthesized by solvent evaporation technique using Compritol 888 and oleic acid, optimised by Box-Behnken design and characterized by FTIR and HR-TEM. The n-value for peppas model was 0.8676 which showed anomalous phenomenon and sustained drug release from FEN-NLCs. Conclusion: The current research conclusively manifested that Fenoprofen Calcium loaded nanostructured lipid carriers-based hydrogel holds great prospective for providing sustained drug release.

TI Impact of internal migration on labor market outcomes: Evidence from
   Ethiopia
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Internal migration; Labor market outcomes; Education; Ethiopia
ID UNEMPLOYMENT; MIGRANTS; DETERMINANTS; IMMIGRATION; ECONOMICS; EDUCATION
AB The movement of people is considered a means of labor market adjustment and reducing fragmentation. This study contributes to the literature by examining the causal effect of internal migration on various labor market outcomes and job quality and showing the role of education in shaping their relationship in a war-affected and developing country context. By using the 2013 and 2021 Ethiopian Labor Force and Migration Surveys (LFMS) and an instrumental variable approach (IV), this study finds a significant and positive effect of internal migration on employment probability; however, the employment gains do not consistently translate into better job quality indicators such as wages, contract types and working hours for all migrants. Importantly, education has a critical role in enhancing the positive influence of internal migration on job quality indicators. The results reveal educated migrants earn significantly higher wages, are more likely to hold permanent contracts and work fewer hours. The disaggregated results further reveal that permanent employment opportunities are limited and mainly benefit male migrants in a few regions, while female migrants work longer hours. The findings also show that the employment effect of internal migration is stronger in urban areas and among male migrants. Overall, the results suggest the necessity of labor market policies that go beyond enhancing the mobility of individuals and integrate education and skills development strategies with migration policy, empower women, and foster inclusive urban labor market institutions.

TI Education, language, and postcolonial legacies in West African
   borderlands: Togolese students in Ghana
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Educational migration; South-South mobility; Borderland education;
   Postcolonial education; Ghana-Togo border
AB This article examines the educational experiences of Togolese migrant students attending public schools in rural Ghanaian border towns, focusing on everyday forms of South-South educational mobility in West Africa. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 40 Togolese students, the study explores why students cross the Ghana-Togo border for schooling, how they navigate differences between the two national education systems, and how they negotiate social integration and identity within Ghanaian schools. The findings show that educational migration in this context is shaped by aspirations to acquire English, access Ghana's fee-free basic education, and avoid institutional barriers such as grade repetition in Togo. While shared ethnic and linguistic ties support social belonging in border communities, they do not guarantee inclusion within schools. Inside classrooms, Englishonly instruction, placement practices, and assessment regimes rooted in postcolonial education systems often devalue prior learning acquired in Francophone contexts, producing institutional exclusion despite social familiarity. At the same time, students actively draw on multilingual repertoires, peer networks, and cross-border knowledge to navigate these constraints, creating limited and uneven forms of hybridity within formal schooling. By integrating Social Integration Theory and Third Space Theory, the article shows that educational integration in borderland contexts is spatially and temporally uneven, shaped by enduring postcolonial language hierarchies. The study contributes to education and development debates by showing how South-South educational mobility challenges assumptions embedded in national education systems and constrains human capital formation, despite regional integration frameworks such as ECOWAS. It argues that maximising the developmental returns of education in border regions requires policy reforms that recognise prior learning, support linguistic flexibility, and value students' transcultural competencies as developmental assets, not as deficits.

TI Girls negotiating schooling after pregnancy in rural Zimbabwe
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Afro-feminist intersectionality; Rural education; School re-entry
   policy; Teenage pregnancy; Zimbabwe
AB Teenage pregnancy continues to disrupt girls' schooling in rural Zimbabwe despite the Education Amendment Act (2020), which guarantees readmission after childbirth. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 22 out-of-school young mothers aged 16-19, this study uses an Afro-feminist intersectional framework to examine how pregnancy reshapes educational trajectories within contexts of poverty, moral regulation, and patriarchal authority. The findings show that school exclusion is rarely the result of formal policy alone. Instead, girls' educational opportunities are shaped by moral judgements about sexual respectability, community surveillance, and the transfer of decision-making power to fathers, husbands, and religious authorities. These relational forms of governance frequently override legal protections, rendering the right to return largely symbolic. At the same time, young mothers continue to pursue education through negotiated and adaptive strategies, including returning for examinations, aligning schooling with seasonal income cycles, sharing childcare with female kin, and combining work with future study. These pathways reflect constrained but persistent aspirations rather than inevitable disengagement. The study argues that school re-entry policies must move beyond legal access to address the social and material conditions that shape educational decision-making. Meaningful inclusion requires financial support, childcare provision, stigma reduction, and flexible learning pathways that recognise young mothers as legitimate learners within their everyday realities.

TI A triadic discourse-identity-affordance framework for scaffolding the
   development of research discourse competence
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
DE Discourse-identity framework; L2 academic writing; Research discourse
   competence; Academic identity; Rhetorical strategy
ID ACADEMIC LITERACIES; KNOWLEDGE; PERSUASION; CHINESE; GENRE
AB Academic writing instruction in EFL contexts has increasingly emphasized genre awareness and rhetorical competence. However, less attention has been paid to how discourse strategies, academic identity, and sociocultural context interact in students' writing development, or how such interaction can be pedagogically operationalized. The present study proposes and implements a multidimensional academic discourse-identity framework that conceptualizes academic writing as the coordinated enactment of discourse strategies (Ethos, Pathos, and Logos), academic identity roles, and sociocultural affordances. The framework was implemented in an English academic writing course for undergraduate engineering students, where instruction guided students to make explicit rhetorical decisions in relation to disciplinary expectations and projected professional identities. To examine how the framework functioned in practice, the study adopts a qualitative research design combining micro-level textual analysis of students' writing with postcourse interviews. Pre- and post-intervention Introduction sections from three students representing different proficiency levels were selected as focal cases. The findings show consistent improvements in rhetorical organization, credibility construction, and authorial positioning. Notably, these developments were observed across proficiency levels, suggesting that discourse awareness and identity enactment can develop alongside, or even prior to, full linguistic accuracy. The study contributes to EAP research by offering a theoretically grounded yet pedagogically actionable framework, and by providing fine-grained discourse evidence of how academic writing competence develops through the interaction of discourse, identity, and context.

TI Evaluative language in sociology lecturers' discourse: An appraisal
   analysis of disciplinary stance in university classrooms
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic lectures; Evaluative language; Appraisal resources;
   Disciplinary discourse; Sociology academic lectures
ID ACADEMIC LECTURES; METADISCOURSE; ENGAGEMENT; RELEVANCE; MODEL
AB This study explores evaluative language in university sociology lectures delivered in English, focusing on how lecturers appraise knowledge and engage students using resources of attitude, engagement, and graduation. Drawing on Martin and White's (2005) appraisal framework, we analysed eight face-to-face lectures to examine the disciplinary and pedagogical functions of evaluation. The findings reveal a clear preference for positive evaluative meanings, particularly in judgement and appreciation, while affect remains relatively infrequent. Engagement is primarily realised through expansive resources, especially first-and second-person pronouns combined with modal verbs and stance expressions, which help construct dialogic space and interpersonal alignment. Graduation resources show extensive use of no-scale and up-scale forms to stabilise reference, foreground significance, and calibrate epistemic commitment, while down-scale resources contribute more selectively to nuance and caution. The study contributes to a more finegrained understanding of evaluative discourse in spoken academic genres and highlights how lecturers use appraisal resources to organise disciplinary meanings, guide interpretation, and support pedagogical interaction. These findings also have implications for disciplinary listening and evaluative awareness in EAP contexts.

TI Rhetorical organization of Discussion sections across research articles,
   master's theses, and doctoral dissertations: A move-based analysis of
   frequency, sequencing, and embedding
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
DE Move analysis; Discussion sections; Move sequencing; Move embedding;
   Postgraduate writing; EAP pedagogy
ID APPLIED LINGUISTICS; METADISCOURSE; ENGLISH; INTRODUCTIONS; CHINESE
AB While prior research has largely focused on move frequency, less is known about how moves interact dynamically across levels of discourse, particularly in postgraduate writing. This study therefore examines the rhetorical organization of Discussion sections across three academic genres in applied linguistics-research articles (RAs), master's theses (MAs), and doctoral dissertations (DDs)-with particular attention to how rhetorical functions are structured, sequenced, and embedded. Drawing on a token-balanced corpus of 87 texts, the study analyses move frequency, move sequencing, and move embedding. The findings reveal that, although all three genres share a common functional core centred on reporting and commenting on results, they differ systematically in rhetorical organization. RAs exhibit the greatest flexibility, characterized by recursive sequencing and dense embedding of multiple commentary functions. DDs display intermediate patterns, with more frequent integration of interpretation and comparison, whereas MAs rely more heavily on linear reporting with limited elaboration. These patterns suggest a developmental progression in Discussion writing, from relatively linear and reporting-oriented structures to more integrated and rhetorically dense forms of argumentation. The study contributes to genre analysis by extending move-based approaches to account for sequencing and embedding as key dimensions of rhetorical organization. It also proposes a revised move-step model for postgraduate Discussion writing, offering an empirically grounded framework for genre-informed EAP pedagogy.

AB This article aims to map and analyze Brazilian academic production on teacher training for the integration of Digital Technologies (DT) in Early Childhood Education (ECE), based on an integrative review in the Brazilian Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations (BDTD) between 2008 and 2023. TI CHALLENGES OF DISTANCE LEARNING: A STUDY ON PARTICIPATION IN<br
   />INTEGRATIVE PROJECTS
SO PERSPECTIVAS EM DIALOGO-REVISTA DE EDUCACAO E SOCIEDADE
LA English
DT Article
DE Distance; Education; Integrative Project
AB The expansion of Distance Education (DE) in Brazilian higher education has broadened access to academic training but also revealed pedagogical challenges, especially regarding student engagement. Practical and collaborative subjects, such as the Integrative Project (IP), require active participation, which becomes problematic due to low attendance in synchronous classes and limited interaction in virtual forums. This study analyzed the relationship between student participation and academic performance in IPs at the Virtual University of the State of S & atilde;o Paulo (UNIVESP), focusing on three classes from different courses. Using a quantitative approach, data from three consecutive semesters were examined, including attendance records, forum interactions, and final group project grades. The sample included students from Production Engineering, Computer Science, and Business Administration. Results showed that groups with higher participation achieved better academic performance, while those with lower engagement obtained significantly lower averages. A direct correlation between engagement and academic achievement was observed. The findings highlight the importance of active pedagogical mediation, consistent interaction, and systematic monitoring by instructors and tutors as essential factors to ensure the effectiveness of Distance Education and the success of Integrative Projects as formative tools.

DT Article

ID EMOTIONAL PRESENCE; TEACHING PRESENCE; LEARNING PRESENCE; SOCIAL
   PRESENCE; GOOGLE SCHOLAR; ONLINE; SCIENCE; FRAMEWORK; TRENDS; SCOPUS
AB The Community of Inquiry (CoI) has provided a useful tool for studying technology-enhanced learning environments. It has also been implemented as the theoretical framework for many types of relevant research. Since its development, the framework has generated substantial interest among scholars in many fields such as distance education, online and blended learning and computed-mediated instruction. Although extensive research has been carried out on the CoI, no single study has been conducted that statistically and mathematically examines all publications of the framework. This study aimed to comprehensively review more than two decades of publications on the CoI framework by applying the bibliometric analysis technique. Therefore, all the corresponding Scopus records (in total 5169) in the past 24 years (1999-2023) were analyzed using the VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, and CiteSpace tools. The study described various essential research indicators, such as the research categories (directions), most productive authors, journals, institutions, and countries, along with potential research hotspots. The thematic analysis highlighted the research themes that have attracted scholars in the field by visualization of the current CoI research landscape.

TI Effect of blended learning on mathematical achievement and anxiety: A
   context-based technology integration for meaningful learning
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Blended learning; technology integration; mathematics anxiety;
   personalized learning; course outcome
ID WORKING-MEMORY; MATH ANXIETY; STUDENTS; MOTIVATION; DESIGN
AB Ethiopia has envisioned becoming a middle-income country in the year 2030. To achieve this vision, several initiatives including the ESDP (I-VI), GQIP, and the education development Roadmap have been undertaken to improve the quality of education at all levels. Apart from those initiatives, it is equally important to rethink of a pedagogical approach that suits the contemporary technological advancement and cultural contexts. Currently, our world is experiencing scientific and technological changes, but the customary methods are relatively unable to cope with these changes. It is no longer viable to rely on one-size-fits-all curriculum. So far, the impact of instructional technology on students learning is not consistent and lacks specific context of students' environment. This indicates that there is a need for intensive investigation to make learning more meaningful and interactive. This study aimed to restructure the existing mathematics course in Ethiopian higher education so as to produce a pedagogically enhanced learning environment. To achieve the goal of the study, a pedagogical intervention with a time series design was made at Wolkite University, Ethiopia. The repeated measures ANOVA show significant difference between students' mean scores of course achievement measured before, during and after the intervention (F (2.182, 52.358) = 8.354, p < .05, eta 2 = 0.258). The multiple comparison test further shows a significant improvement of students' mathematical achievement. It was also found that when technology was used as a tool to enhance students learning, it can overcome the math anxiety caused by the cognitive failure. Therefore, blended learning could be a good approach to enhance students' mathematics achievement. This might also be extended at lower levels. Additional imperative implications for practice and future research are forwarded.

TI From informal to formal - A case study about the impact of distant
   learning on formative feedback in Danish schools
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Covid-19; distant learning; digital platforms; assessment; feedback
   practice
AB Even though Denmark is a highly digitized country, the COVID-19 pandemic has pushed schools to adopt extreme forms of distant learning, as everything should be conducted online through digital platforms. Our study aims at analysing the impact of distant learning practice on feedback practice, from the perspective of teachers and pupils. More specifically we focus on pupils in Danish mid-school, who are subject to a final exam to qualify for access to high school. We have conducted a netnographic inquiry, combining virtual observations and interviews with teachers and pupils. Our results show that the new distant learning practice prevented teachers to engage in non-formal assessment and feedback practice, such as spontaneous walks across the classrooms and dialogue with pupils on their difficulties, hence making it hard to keep an overview on their pupils' progress. To compensate for the lack of non-formal feedback practices, distant learning has turned feedback practices into formal evaluations, leading the pupils to feel under pressure and less engaged in their learning. Our study provides an original perspective regarding specific aspects, such as feedback practices, which require forms of spontaneous dialogue between teachers and pupils and are central for learning, hence providing meaningful insights for the implementation of distant learning in mid school and the importance of a close dialogue between pupils and teachers.

   technical education teachers in Nigerian tertiary institutions
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA

DT Article
DE Technology-enhanced learning; vocational and technical education;
   E-learning; information and communications technology
AB The study determined training needs of teachers and issues in the utilization of Technology-enhanced Learning tools in Vocational and Technical Education in Nigerian tertiary institutions. Five research questions and one hypothesis guided the study. The sample for the study is 318 teachers from six tertiary institutions that offer majority of Vocational and Technical Education programmes in Nigeria. Instrument for data collection was developed by the researchers and was validated by five experts in Vocational and Technical Education. The overall reliability index of the instrument is 0.81. TI Students online learning experience during emergency remote teaching in
   higher education
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Covid-19; emergency remote teaching; higher education; online learning;
   technology
ID CHALLENGES; COVID-19
AB For actionable insight, this study explored computer science and information technology students' online learning experience in an emergency remote teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic in a public technical university in Ghana. A mixed method research of both quantitative and qualitative design was used to expand the evidence base. The inherent set of factors of the learning experience were determined by an exploratory factor analysis and confirmed with a multiple regression. Six factors comprising sense of concern, institutional support, effective communication, connectedness, mediated technologies, and stress levels explained 66.5% of the variance in the patterns of relationship. All factors had positive regression weights and added significantly to the prediction. Potentials identified comprised positive reactions to institutional support, improved lecturer-student interaction, active participation, accessible course contents, and moderately high future online learning expectations. The challenges included unpreparedness, unreliable Internet, high cost of data, and incidental learning design and pedagogy. Evidently, the higher education landscape shifted during the pandemic in obvious ways to merit further studies and reflective online learning administration to inform robust technology-oriented post-pandemic practices.

TI What is important and why? Students' experience of educational
   activities including technologies
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Digital technologies; educational activities; engagement; on-campus
   courses; students experience
AB Digital technology is now a central part of higher education and has led to high expectations of increased student activity, engagement, and learning. Drawing on two research projects about Norwegian bachelor's students, this article explores how they experience educational activities, including the use of technologies in on-campus courses. It is vital to understand this from the students' point of view. Data have been gathered from qualitative group interviews and an online survey. The analysis draws on socio-cultural perspectives on learning, focusing on what forms of activities and technologies the students experienced as important and useful, or challenging, in various contexts. The results suggest that, despite extensive access to digital technologies, the students experience that activities that support physical encounters on campus, such as lectures and group work, are more important and beneficial than flexible digital solutions. Technologies are basically experienced as a supplement for handling academic demands. The possible implications this has for students' experiences of educational activities and technology use, and teachers' facilitation, are discussed. The overall intention is to highlight the significance of the students' experiences, as well as contribute to more realistic institutional expectations for the pedagogical use of technology.

TI Understanding students' perceived need satisfaction, enjoyment, and
   participation intention in a leaderboard-based math practice game
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Gamification; leaderboard; math education; self-determination theory;
   motivation
ID INTRINSIC MOTIVATION; GAMIFICATION; TASK; DESIGN
AB Though many studies suggest the positive effects of leaderboard on participants' learning and motivation, research also shows that not all students benefit from the use of leaderboard. Based on self-determination theory (SDT), this study examined how students' actual competence, perceived competence, perceived autonomy, and perceived relatedness affected students' enjoyment and intention for future participation in a leaderboard-based math practice game. The results showed that both perceived competence and perceived autonomy were closely related to students' enjoyment and intention for future participation, while students' actual competence and perceived relatedness were not related to their enjoyment or intention for future participation in such leaderboard-based math practice games. The findings of the study offer valuable insights and recommendations for both gamification research and practice.

TI Analysis of self-regulated learning strategies used by online learners
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Blended learning; online learning; self-regulated learning strategies;
   self-regulated learning
ID MOTIVATION
AB This study is a qualitative survey research that examines the self-regulated learning strategies used by students in the blended online learning process. Participants were made up of 67 pre-service teachers studying at a faculty of education. A questionnaire form was used to determine students' self-regulated learning strategies. The self-regulated learning strategies were classified under three themes: before the lesson, during the lesson, and after the lesson. The strategies used before the lessons were organizing the environment, planning, motivating oneself, and physiological and psychological readiness. During the online lessons, students used strategies such as taking notes, attention focusing, help seeking, effort management, self-discipline, taking a break, and time management. After the lessons, students used strategies such as reviewing records, organizing and transforming, practicing, working with additional resources, help seeking, self-testing, and completing tasks. Furthermore, the study results that were revealed to be different from the results of similar studies were discussed and recommendations for future studies were made. In addition, the study revealed that the strategies used by the students differed according to their communication modes. While synchronous and blended groups used more self-regulated learning strategies, asynchronous students used less self-regulated learning strategies.

AB In a traditional classroom environment, listening comprehension plays a vital role in enabling students to actively participate in the learning process. This is because a significant portion of information is conveyed through the instructor's explanations and class discussions. Developing strong listening skills can help students effectively understand and participate in classroom activities. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of flipped listening classroom on undergraduate English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students' foreign language listening anxiety and willingness to communicate. A sample of 46 students at a public university in Iran was chosen to participate in the study using convenience sampling. Implementing a quasi-experimental pretest posttest control group design, two intact classes were randomly assigned to flipped and traditional lecture-based groups. The findings of the study revealed that flipped listening classroom had a positive impact on alleviating foreign language listening anxiety of EFL students and increasing their willingness to communicate. The study has some implications for the material developers, English instructors and students.

Makerere University, a venerable institution in the region, was not exempt from this directive. This study delivers valuable perspectives for developers of eLearning systems, emphasizing the importance of creating user-friendly platforms that enhance the learner experience. TI Smart teaching versus hard teaching: Insights from instructors from old
   and new classrooms in Ghana
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Smart classroom; smart learning; smart learning environment; smart
   teaching; traditional learning environment
ID LEARNING-ENVIRONMENT; SCHOOL ENVIRONMENT; TEACHERS; STUDENTS; EDUCATION
AB Smart learning environment (SLE) modules are rapidly expanding with the advancement of technology. However, the concept is still new to many educational institutions in developing countries, with scant studies conducted using the African context. To avoid being left behind in the steps towards modernization, the qualitative study proposes the need to migrate from a traditional learning environment (TLE) to a SLE. Thirty-eight (38) teachers in Ghana who transitioned from TLE to a SLE were recruited to explore their pedagogical experiences in instructing in TLE (old classrooms) and SLE (new classrooms). Generally, teachers favoured SLE compared to TLE. Teachers were motivated to instruct in smart schools because of the affordances of smart technologies. They considered the ambience created in SLE as conducive to promoting their psychological well-being, facilitating their professional development, fostering good assessment strategies, and building twenty-first-century skills in learners needed in the labour market. However, a majority of the teachers perceived self-regulation and social interactions to be more effective in TLE. The key challenges in the SLE included network lag, limited funds to purchase data bundles, malfunction of learning management systems (LMS), and difficulty in designing a Smart App tailored to instructors' and students' interests. It is recommended that school administrators and policymakers continually revise SLE frameworks for a successful smart education. Future researchers can investigate how to promote personalized and adaptive learning in SLE and promising tools to assist instructors in technology-enhanced learning environments.

TI The impacts of implementing e-blended learning approach (e-BLA) in
   communicative english language skills I course: Focused on Wolaita Sodo
   University, Ethiopia
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Communicative english language skills 1 course; conventional modes of
   instruction; EFL instructors; e-blended learning approach; e-learning;
   speaking skills' achievement
AB This study dealt with the impacts of implementing an e-blended learning approach (e-BLA) in communicative English language skills 1 (CELS1) course to achieve English speaking skills (ESS). Hence, the pre & post-test design of a quasi-experimental study was employed. The informants were two sections' 102 students (50 & 52) who were categorized under comparison & treatment groups to pass through CMI & an e-BLA respectively. The tools were then tests, classroom observation & FGD. Six among the treatment group were selected for the FGD. The quantitative data of independent & paired samples t-tests were utilized to determine the significant differences of inter & intragroup between an e-BLA & CMI at 0.05 (5%) alpha level. The qualitative data of FGD & observations were thematically analyzed in a statement form. Hence, the mean comparison of pretest scores in independent samples t-test (53.02 & 54.19) reveals the absence of significant difference of scores between the two groups before intervention. However, after the intervention, the treatment group outscored (70.81) significantly higher (p < .05) than the comparison group (55.56) on SST. Similarly, the paired samples t-test indicated the magnitude of the posttest (70.81) over the pre (54.19) with the effect size -3.4. Likewise, the qualitative data revealed the informants achieved ESS better in e-BLA than CMI. Therefore, Ethiopian educational curriculum should consider e-integrated instructions in all subjects & all levels.

An experiment was conducted to evaluate the proposed setup followed by a student attitude survey. The results show the portal's leverage in reducing the time required to fix errors and the number of compilation attempts. The survey indicates a positive response.

TI Supporting visually impaired students in virtual learning environments
   in Ghana
SO E-LEARNING AND DIGITAL MEDIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Ghana; inequalities; accessibility4Equity framework; A4ESupportive
   framework; visually impaired students
AB Distance education (DE) has been in existence in Ghana for almost three decades guided by the philosophy of making quality education more accessible and relevant to all students. In line with best practices across the globe, Ghanaian institutions providing DE have been integrating digital technologies to augment traditional forms of delivery over the last decade. However, specific gaps have been identified in the provision for students with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). To address this, the current study involves a multi-site exploratory case study using Accessibility4Equity principles to explore the challenges that distance providers face when enrolling visually impaired students (VIS). Arising from this, recommendations suggest that future research is needed to address the gaps in the Accessibility4Equity supportive framework for VIS in virtual learning spaces.

TI Patterns of Play in Young Children Developing With Delays
SO INFANTS & YOUNG CHILDREN
LA English
DT Article
DE children with delays; development; play development; typically
   developing children; young children
ID PRETEND PLAY; JOINT ATTENTION; SYMBOLIC PLAY; REPRESENTATIONAL PLAY;
   FUNCTIONAL PLAY; OBJECT PLAY; AUTISM; COMMUNICATION; ENGAGEMENT;
   TODDLERS
AB This paper examined object play in a new cross-sectional sample of 203 children developing with delays using a highly differentiated set of play categories to provide more detailed descriptions of these developments. Thirty-minute videotaped observations of children playing with a caregiver in their homes were taken at 8, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, and 60 months of age. Participants included children with: autism (n = 38); Down syndrome (n = 27); language delays (n = 55); delays in one or more other domains (n = 76); and children born prematurely (n = 7). Play activities were coded into 21 qualitatively different categories and analyzed in terms of frequency of activities and variety of examples expressed within categories. These children's play activities were compared to a sample of 289 typically developing (TD) children, observed contemporaneously at the same age points. The groups were comparable in frequency. The children with delays expressed the same play categories as the TD children, but expressed more complex categories at later age points with less variety. Particular difficulties were identified for children with autism and children with Down syndrome. Implications for assessment and intervention center on evaluation using differentiated play categories, determining variety within them, and setting goals based on a developmental model.

   Exposed to Opioids
SO INFANTS & YOUNG CHILDREN
LA English
DT Article
DE developmental outcomes; neonatal abstinence syndrome; neonatal opioid
   withdrawal syndrome; parental substance use disorder; pediatric

ID VISUAL ANALOG SCALE; USE DISORDER; INFORMANT DISCREPANCIES;
   BUPRENORPHINE; OUTCOMES; PSYCHOPATHOLOGY; METHADONE; DELIVERY
AB The purpose of this study is to explore sensory processing patterns in children aged 3-5 years with a history of prenatal opioid exposure (POE). A cohort of 61 children participated in comprehensive evaluations at a multidisciplinary clinic. Sensory processing issues were identified as a common concern based on a shared decision-making tool completed by caregivers. TI Supporting Multisector Infant-Early Childhood Mental Health Professional
   Development: Evaluation of the Core Curriculum
SO INFANTS & YOUNG CHILDREN
LA English
DT Article
DE early intervention; infant early childhood mental health; professional
   development; reflective practice; training
ID REFLECTIVE SUPERVISION; EARLY INTERVENTION; TOXIC STRESS; MODEL
AB Infant early childhood mental health (IECMH) professional development is recommended for early intervention and early childhood special education (ECSE) professionals to support their relationship-based work with families and enhance their efforts to promote social-emotional development. As a result, access to evidence-based, comprehensive, competency-based IECMH training that supports infant early childhood professional knowledge and practice is a priority. The Michigan Association for Infant Mental Health designed and implemented the Foundation for Culturally Sensitive, Relationship-focused IECMH Practice Training Series: Core Curriculum to address this need for Part C providers, ECSE professionals, Early Head Start/Head Start staff, and IECMH home visiting therapists. Evidence also suggests the training may have increased impacts for cohorts limited to early interventionists and ECSE professionals, particularly those with no previous IECMH training or reflective supervision experience. The Core Curriculum is unique in its comprehensive, competency-based content, interactive design, multi-sector relevance, evaluated impact on IECMH practice and knowledge, and accessible implementation.

TI Content Validity of the Assessment, Evaluation, And Programming System
   (AEPS) for Infants And Children 3rd Edition in Spain

DT Article
DE authentic assessment; content validity; family centered practices
AB This study investigated the content validity of the Assessment, Evaluation, and Programming System (AEPS) for Infants and Children-Third Edition (AEPS-3) in Spain. TI Leveraging learner individual differences in data-driven learning:
   Introducing the special issue
SO LEARNING AND INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Data-driven learning; Corpora; Individual differences; Working memory;
   Motivation; Self-regulation; Digital literacy; Corpus literacy; Language
   education
ID LANGUAGE
AB Data-driven learning (DDL), where learners explore authentic language data (often via corpora or concordancers) to induce patterns, has matured from a niche methodology into a versatile approach supporting language awareness, genre literacy, and disciplinary communication. Yet outcomes of DDL are notably variable: Some learners thrive in discovery-oriented environments, while others experience cognitive overload, frustration, or superficial pattern matching. We can see rather clearly from the papers in this collection and published research elsewhere how research and theory on learner individual differences (IDs) shape engagement with and benefits from DDL, including language proficiency, metalinguistic awareness, cognitive abilities (working memory, attention control), learning preferences, affective factors (motivation, anxiety, tolerance of ambiguity), self-regulation, and digital/corpus literacy. We would like to propose an integrative framework linking IDs to DDL task demands, tool affordances, and instructional design choices. We conclude with pedagogical principles for adaptive DDL, offering strategies for differentiation, scaffolding, and assessment, and outlining future research directions for robust, equity-minded implementation in diverse educational contexts.

TI Understanding the factors associated with youths' NEET status in
   humanitarian settings in Bangladesh
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Youth NEET; FDMN; Education; Employment; Training; Gender disparities
ID SOCIAL EXCLUSION; EDUCATION; TRANSITION
AB Countries with a high proportion of young people not in education, employment or training (NEET) experience substantial loss of potential productivity and economic growth. In Bangladesh, 34.3% of the youth population is classified as NEET, with higher prevalence in humanitarian settings where host and Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMN) coexist. This study provides one of the largest comparative analyses of NEET young people across host and displaced youth in a protracted humanitarian setting. It investigates factors associated with NEET status among young people aged 14-25 years (inclusive) in Cox's Bazar. A cross-sectional survey of 22,114 youths from Teknaf Upazila, collected during August-November 2024, was used to identify factors associated with youth NEET status. The descriptive analysis showed higher NEET rates among FDMN youths (66.6%) compared to hosts (43.7%), and a pronounced gender divide between women (72.8%) and men (19.6%). These disparities reflect structural constraints in the surveyed area, including legally restricted formal employment and schooling for FDMN populations. In addition, these intersect with gender norms which limit young women's economic participation. Regression analysis indicated that higher levels of educational attainment were significantly associated with lower NEET prevalence and reduced gender disparities. Vocational training was associated with a reduced likelihood of being NEET among women but not men. However, despite the substantial data set, given the cross-sectional nature of the data, these findings are associative and cannot imply causality. Findings underscore the need for targeted secondary education and gender-responsive training initiatives tailored to both FDMN and host youths to address community and gender-based inequalities in labour market participation.

TI Beyond the average: A machine learning typology for differentiated
   foundational learning in Somaliland
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Foundational learning; Learner profiles; Unsupervised machine learning;
   Educational data mining; EGRA and EGMA; Somaliland
AB This study examines whether national early-grade assessment data can reveal hidden variation in foundational learning in Somaliland. Using unsupervised machine learning, specifically K-means clustering, the study analyzed 5403 Grade 3 learners across 19 literacy and numeracy indicators derived from the Early Grade Reading Assessment and Early Grade Mathematics Assessment. Four distinct and educationally interpretable learner profiles were identified: Globally Advanced (26.9%), Globally At-Risk (16.5%), Advanced Literacy with Calculation Gaps (34.0%), and Numeracy-Oriented with Literacy Gaps (22.6%). The results show that learner differences were not limited to a single high-low continuum. Instead, two large dissociated profiles revealed uneven development across literacy and numeracy domains. Demographic analysis showed significant associations between learner profile membership and school location, school ownership, and gender, with the strongest pattern linked to school location. The Globally At-Risk profile was the only majority-rural group and had the highest concentration of public-school learners. These findings show that national assessment data can support more differentiated diagnosis and targeted intervention in low-resource education systems.

TI The impact of international mobility to established democracies on
   Russian young people's aspirations to engage socio-politically in Russia
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE International student mobility; Russia; Socio-political participation;
   Democratisation
ID STUDENT MOBILITY; EUROPEAN IDENTITY; SOFT POWER; MIGRATION; REPRESSION;
   EDUCATION; BEHAVIOR; YOUTH
AB The extant literature often frames international education in democratic societies as a driver of socio-political development and emphasises its transformative, 'democratising' influence on both the mobile student and their country of origin. Building on such assumptions, this paper investigates the impact of studying in established democracies on Russian young people's aspirations to engage socio-politically in Russia. The analysis draws on data from 55 in-depth interviews with Russian students and alumni of UK and US universities. The findings challenge the widespread association of educational migration to politically developed states with shifts in mobile students' political behaviours and their potential to bring about socio-political change. More specifically, the evidence in this research project points to the paramount importance of the sending country's sociopolitical context in considering the linkage between student migrants' democratic socialisation abroad and ambitions to exercise political agency. The unfavourable political environment in Russia discourages young people from engaging in political activities, and their priorities lie in the private sphere. Only a small minority admitted the influence of mobility on their current or potential future political participation. With regards to intentions to get involved in social/civic initiatives, international mobility does seem to have certain influence on Russian youth. Such aspirations were usually manifest in envisaging small-scale and non-confrontational projects in the fields of education, recycling or volunteering.

TI Rhetorical complexity in case analysis writing: A corpus-informed study
   of the advisory move
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
DE Case analysis writing; Advisory reasoning; Genre-based pedagogy;
   Swalesian move analysis; Undergraduate writing
ID GENRE
AB This study examines how undergraduate students construct the Advisory move in case analysis writing, the rhetorical move in which disciplinary analysis is transformed into actionable recommendations. While prior research has mapped the overall structure of business case reports and provided detailed accounts of the Options and Alternatives move, the Advisory move itself remains comparatively under-described. Drawing on Swalesian move analysis, we investigate the internal rhetorical organization of the Advisory move. Using a 256,385-word sub-corpus of business and information systems texts drawn from the British Academic Written English (BAWE) corpus and the Information Systems Writing in the Middle East (ISWIME) corpus, we developed and validated a detailed coding scheme of Advisory sub-moves and steps. The analysis identifies three core sub-moves, Orientation, Recommendation, and Argument, which are realized through steps such as endorsement, rejection, implementation, justification, conditionality, and limitation. Frequency and range analyses show that recommendation and justification are obligatory components of advisory writing, while other steps function as optional resources for nuance and contingency. By making visible the rhetorical structure through which students formulate and justify recommendations, this study extends existing genre descriptions of case analysis writing and provides an empirical foundation for genre-based pedagogy.

TI Teaching EAP for the digital age: practitioner voices from a
   pre-sessional programme
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
DE English for academic purposes; Pre-sessional programmes; Online
   learning; Emergency remote teaching; Practitioner perspectives; Higher
   education
ID LISTENING COMPREHENSION; TEACHERS ATTITUDES; FLIPPED CLASSROOM;
   LANGUAGE; ONLINE; VIDEO; MEDIA
AB The shift to online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic significantly transformed English for Academic Purposes (EAP) instruction. Pre-sessional programmes, traditionally delivered on campus, moved online under Emergency Remote Teaching (ERT), raising questions about how EAP can be effectively taught virtually. While existing research has addressed technology use in language education, limited attention has been given to EAP practitioners' experiences during this critical period. This study addresses that gap through a case study offering an emic perspective on how practitioners perceived their teaching and students' development of academic language and skills in an online pre-sessional. The study also highlights increasing digital pedagogical confidence among practitioners and points to a possible shift toward online and blended delivery models in such programmes. Nonetheless, it highlights the need for targeted curriculum re-design and professional development to support effective EAP instruction online. By foregrounding practitioner perspectives, the study contributes to an underexplored area of EAP research and offers implications for the future of digital EAP provision in higher education.

AB This scoping review moves beyond the advocacy to ungrading alone to systematically map the theory and practice of this concept in second language (L2) writing instruction. TI Structural dimensions of a digital learning ecosystem for research
   skills in secondary education
SO CONTEMPORARY EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE research skills; digital learning ecosystem; secondary education;
   project-based learning; educational technology; inquiry-based learning
AB Despite widespread digital access in secondary education, students continue to demonstrate limited capacity for systematic inquiry, critical source evaluation, and evidence-based reasoning-a paradox that existing virtual learning environments have failed to resolve. This article presents the structural dimensions of a conceptual digital learning ecosystem (DLE) designed to strengthen research skills in secondary education, based on a scoping review of 34 studies published between 2019 and 2025. TI Interactional voice construction in academic research articles across
   disciplines and part-genres
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
ID LEXICAL BUNDLES; L2 WRITERS; METADISCOURSE; SCIENCE; STANCE; SECTIONS;
   ENGLISH; FRAMES; MOVES
AB While prior research has examined how interactional voice varies across disciplines or article sections, few studies have explored the intersection of these dimensions, especially in the social sciences, where voice expectations are diverse and often implicit. This study investigates how interactional voice is constructed through metadiscourse markers and interactional lexical bundles across three social science disciplines (applied linguistics, economics, and psychology) and four research article part-genres (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion). Drawing on a corpus of 240 published articles, we quantified the use of hedges, boosters, attitude markers, and directives using the Authorial Voice Analyzer (AVA), and identified high-frequency lexical bundles containing these features. Results show that part-genre exerts a stronger influence on voice construction than discipline, with interaction effects indicating that disciplinary differences vary across part-genres. The Discussion section exhibited the highest frequency of voice markers, while the Methods section showed the lowest. Disciplinary differences were more modest, with psychology articles featuring fewer boosters and more attitude markers than the other disciplines. Lexical bundle analysis further revealed section-specific formulaic patterns of stance. These findings suggest that voice in academic writing is shaped more by local rhetorical purpose than by disciplinary identity. They support pedagogical practices that emphasize both discipline-and genre-sensitive instruction in EAP, specifically through explicit teaching of stance strategies and recurrent lexical bundles.

TI A National Survey of Pharmacy Skills Laboratory Faculty Perceptions of
   Evaluation, Promotion, and Workload Policies
SO AMERICAN JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Skills laboratory; Faculty; Workload; Workload policies; Equity
AB Objective: The study assessed perceptions of workload and evaluation policies among pharmacy skills laboratory faculty. Methods: A survey was developed and disseminated to American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP) Skills Laboratory Special Interest Group faculty members. The survey contained questions on faculty and institution demographics, satisfaction with current workload, and perceptions of fairness, transparency, workload policy and calculator parity, and promotion climate. Quantitative data were reported using descriptive statistics; exploratory factor analysis assessed item structure, and regression models were used to examine predictors of workload satisfaction. Qualitative data were analyzed using an inductive thematic approach. Results: A total of 75 faculty members from 66 of 130 institutions (response rate [RR], 50.7%) responded. Perceptions of fairness were the strongest predictor of overall satisfaction. Free responses highlighted invisible workload requirements, including concerns related to time, equity, and understanding. Conclusion: This study is among the first to examine skills laboratory faculty perceptions of workload policies, evaluation processes, and promotion climate across a national sample. These findings underscore the importance of developing workload policies and evaluation processes that reflect the unique contributions of skills laboratory faculty to pharmacy education.

TI QuillBot in L2 writing: Implications for assessment in the age of AI
SO ASSESSING WRITING
LA English
DT Article
DE QuillBot; Technology; L2 writing assessment
AB The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools into second language (L2) writing has generated both pedagogical opportunities and assessment-related concerns. While recent research has centered on generative chatbots, QuillBot has emerged as a widely used tool with potential for paragraph-level writing instruction in intensive composition contexts. This techfocused review, therefore, synthesizes empirical studies on the use of QuillBot in L2 writing contexts alongside a critical analysis of the tool's functionalities to inform teachers' effective integration of the tool and assessment of student writing. Accordingly, QuillBot can support linguistic accuracy, lexical variation, and learner confidence, particularly when used as a revision aid during formative stages of writing. However, its sentence-level focus and automated paraphrasing functions may complicate the assessment of originality, independent writing ability, higher-order writing skills, and contextual meaning. From a writing assessment perspective, the tech review suggests that product-oriented evaluation alone may not fully capture students' writing development in AI-assisted contexts. Instead, assessment practices could incorporate process evidence, reflective engagement, and explicit guidance on the ethical use of AI to support rhetorical awareness, learner development, and fairness in assessment. These are presented as implications for writing teachers and students, followed by directions for future research.

TI Reassessing automated essay scoring with large language models: Evidence
   from API and GUI interfaces
SO ASSESSING WRITING
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence; Generative AI; Automated essay scoring; Large
   language model; API; GUI; Temperature
AB Some prior studies on large language model (LLM)-based AES have relied on application programming interfaces (APIs), which may not always reflect classroom use by non-programmers who typically interact with LLMs through graphical user interfaces (GUIs). The present study evaluated the performance of automated essay scoring (AES) by examining two operational variables: the control interface (APIs vs. GUIs) and the temperature setting, which governs the randomness of LLM responses. In this study, 404 s-language English essays were scored by human raters and ChatGPT-4-0613 under three conditions: an API-based approach with a temperature of 0, an API-based approach with a temperature of 1, and a GUI-based approach. Agreement between the API-based and GUI-based approaches ranged from low to moderate. Furthermore, the API-based approach with a temperature of 0 showed closer alignment with human scoring than the API-based approach with a temperature of 1 and the GUI-based approach. Among the LLM raters, the API-based approach with a temperature of 0 was the most consistent, followed by the API-based approach with a temperature of 1 and then the GUI-based approach. These findings underscore the importance of selecting LLM configurations based on assessment contexts and transparently reporting operational parameters, with both theoretical and practical implications.

TI Examining the relevance of three TOEFL Essentials writing tasks to the
   accounting profession: The role of domain experts
SO ASSESSING WRITING
LA English
DT Article
DE Domain experts; Linguistic laypeople; Relevance to TLU domain; Test
   validation
AB Large-scale English language proficiency tests are increasingly used to make decisions about professional registration despite not originally being developed to make predictions about language use in the workplace. Domain experts can play a valuable role as informants in establishing the relevance of test tasks to a specific TLU domain. However, this practice has seldom been critically examined. In particular, no studies to date have examined the nature of the interview questions used when engaging with domain experts in this type of research. The current study was designed with two aims: to (1) explore the relevance of three writing tasks (i.e., Build a Sentence, Write for an Academic Discussion, Write an Email) from the TOEFL Essentials test to the accounting profession and (2) evaluate the judgements of domain expert participants. Twenty accountants from non-English speaking backgrounds as well as three accounting educators were interviewed for the study, drawing on a methodology with broad, general questions. The data was analysed qualitatively to identify (a) to what extent the participants considered the three tasks relevant and (b) what task features they attended to when commenting on the relevance of the tasks. The findings showed that the participants generally found the Build a Sentence the least relevant of the three writing tasks, and the Write an Email task the most relevant. When reviewing the task features the participants judged as relevant to writing demands in their workplace, it was shown they focused on a small/narrow range of features. They also engaged in 'misinterpretations', comparing aspects of test and workplace tasks that did not align (e.g., comparing a writing task to events in a spoken meeting). The findings are discussed in terms of domain expert involvement in validation research.
